title: Keep America Out of War convention and Marxism
summary: Perhanis asks about Rose's politics. Rose was a delegate to the 1938 anti-war convention in Washington and calls himself a classical Marxist and economic determinist.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: In live performance, yeah. Well, I want to ask you a little bit about your social and political philosophy. You might not think you have one particularly, but I think you do.

Okay, fine. Well, and then I want to relate it back to the music. But, well, let me just mention a few things that I picked up from an interview that you did a couple years ago with Dick Allen and asked you about this. From that interview, I understand that you were a delegate to the Keep America on a War Convention.
And... That was in Washington in 1938.
All right. I'm going to ask you a little bit about that.

And I also understand... Well, maybe we ought to start with that and then we'll go on to some other things. But you were a member of the Keep the War... Keep the War... Keep America on a War Convention. And what exactly was that?

Well, it was what it says it was. That it was a coalition of groups of people in America that were eager to block the entrance of the United States into World War II. Are you pacifistic? Am I a pacifist? No, I'm a revolutionary socialist. I'm an orthodox Marxist.
That does not mean a Stalinist, Russian, Maoist Marxist. I am a classical Marxist.
Okay. I know that when we were talking the other night before we went to see Armand Hug that you said that you call yourself an economic determinist.
And a dialectic materialist. Now, I was going to ask you, do you mean this in the Marxian sense?
